newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WILLS TO RESUME TRADING ON FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WILLS TO RESUME TRADING ON FRIDAY.

text.p: Tobacco group W.D. & H.O. Wills Holdings Ltd, which had sought a trading halt in response to the government's new excise plans, said on Thursday that its shares would resume trading on Friday.

The company said it believed there were enormous uncertainties about the management of the new excise regime which it estimated would increase Commonwealth revenue from excise on tobacco products by A$500 million.

The goverment on Thursday gazetted a new excise rate of A$251.27 per kilogram of tobacco in response to the High Court ruling earlier this week which abolished the franchise fees applied by the six states and two territories as unconstitutional. The new excise rate represented a rise of 200 percent, Wills said.

Some states might not pass on the excess revenue to manufacturers and wholesalers and the value rather than quantity basis of the new excise meant that tobacco producers must potentially bear the "A$500 million impost" for at least an unspecified period.
Wills, which is majority-owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc, is one of two listed tobacco companies in Australia.
Its competitors in the local market are Rothmans Holdings Ltd and Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Wills shares last traded at A$2.00 each on Wednesday, 55 cents off the 1997 high and only seven cents off the year's low.
